email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do sewer line replacements?
why_this_wording: Izzy's original pick. Plain, physical, and every plumber knows the job and the margin on it.

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do whole-home repipes?
why_this_wording: "Repipe" is the word plumbers use themselves; homeowners say it too.

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do water main replacements?
why_this_wording: Unambiguous and no jargon. Pairs naturally with sewer line work.

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do tankless water heater installs?
why_this_wording: High volume as well as high ticket, so the honest answer is almost always yes.

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do trenchless sewer line replacements?
typical_us_price: within the $4,000 - $15,000 sewer range, usually the top half
why_this_wording: Sharper, higher-ticket wording of #1 and a good A/B pair against it.
watch_out: Not every plumber owns the equipment, so expect more "no" replies than #1

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do electrical panel upgrades?
why_this_wording: The best single bet in this niche: big ticket and no electrician will say they don't do it.

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do whole-home rewires?
why_this_wording: Biggest residential ticket in the trade, and the phrase is used verbatim on the job.

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do whole-house generator installs?
why_this_wording: Says standby generator without the word "standby", which homeowners don't use.

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do EV charger installs?
why_this_wording: Highest-volume yes in the niche. Roughly 1 in 5 of these jobs turns into a panel upgrade too.
watch_out: Lowest ticket of the five on its own

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do 200 amp service upgrades?
why_this_wording: Same job as #1 in the trade's own words. Run it against #1 to see which wording pulls.
watch_out: Tests wording, not a different service

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do full system replacements?
why_this_wording: The core money job in HVAC. Guaranteed yes, biggest average ticket.

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do AC replacements?
why_this_wording: The plainest possible wording of the same money. Best A/B pair against #1.

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do heat pump installs?
how_widely_offered: most, and growing fast on rebates
why_this_wording: Rebate-driven demand, so owners are actively chasing these jobs right now.

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do new ductwork?
why_this_wording: Two words, zero ambiguity, and it is the line item that turns a $7k job into a $16k one.

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do mini split installs?
why_this_wording: "Mini split" is what the trade and homeowners both say; "ductless" is the brochure word.

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do termite treatments?
why_this_wording: Highest-value recurring work in pest, and the phrase every operator uses.

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do bed bug heat treatments?
why_this_wording: One-visit job at a four-figure ticket. Owners who do it are proud of it and reply.
watch_out: Not universal, heat equipment is a real investment

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do rodent exclusion?
why_this_wording: Trade-standard term for sealing a house up. Instantly understood inside the industry.
watch_out: Slightly more inside-baseball than the others

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do crawl space encapsulation?
why_this_wording: Highest average ticket on this list.
watch_out: Only makes sense where homes have crawl spaces, so segment the list by region

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do termite tenting?
why_this_wording: Very high ticket and very concrete.
watch_out: Mostly Florida, California and the Gulf. Dead variable in most of the Midwest and Northeast

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do full home window replacements?
why_this_wording: The whole-house job, not the one-window job. This is where the money is in this niche.

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do sliding patio door replacements?
why_this_wording: Everyone pictures the same thing instantly, and the multi-panel versions are five figures.

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do bay window installs?
typical_us_price: ~$5,000 for a large bay or bow
why_this_wording: Single highest-ticket individual window. Concrete and visual.

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do hurricane impact windows?
typical_us_price: $700 - $2,875 per window, $1,000 - $1,400 per opening in Miami-Dade
why_this_wording: In coastal markets this is the highest ticket in the trade and owners chase it hard.
watch_out: Florida, Texas and the Gulf only. Useless in Utah, where our current list is

email_line: Hi {{firstName}}, do you do egress window installs?
why_this_wording: Basement and code-driven work, bigger than a standard window swap.
watch_out: Price not verified yet, and it needs a basement market
